headline: Profit jumps on tariff refund; guidance tops long-term goal
summary_short: Cardinal Health's fourth-quarter revenue rose 6% y/y to $63.7B on branded and specialty pharma growth; GAAP diluted EPS jumped 70% to $1.70, aided by a $100M one-time IEEPA tariff-refund recognition in GMPD, while non-GAAP diluted EPS rose 40% to $2.91.
summary_long: Fourth-quarter revenue rose 6% y/y to $63.7B, led by 6% growth in Pharmaceutical and Specialty Solutions on branded and specialty pharma sales. GAAP diluted EPS rose 70% to $1.70 and non-GAAP diluted EPS rose 40% to $2.91, both aided by a $100M one-time IEEPA tariff-refund recognition in the GMPD segment (excluding that item, non-GAAP EPS grew 25% to $2.60). GMPD revenue fell 2% on lower distribution volumes and refund repayments to customers. Cash rose to $4,856M from $3,874M a year earlier; the shareholders' deficit widened modestly to $2,883M. The board approved a $5.0B buyback-authorization increase, and the company initiated FY2027 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $12.40-$12.60 (+13% to +15% growth), above its long-term target.
